about: The package's 20 sources (sources.json; Research-sources.md) against the shared source library (shared/specialization/sources/forearm.ts, forearmMappings.ts; 71 keys) and the app's trainingEvidence.ts. Matched by DOI, PubMed id and URL, never by title alone. 'searchCheck' is what a web search showed on 21 Oct 2026 (page fetches are refused here); it is the evidence a source note would need under 03-anatomy-evidence.md section 1 and 10-multi-region.md section 8.
packageNotes: There is no S01: the package's ids run A01, A02, S02-S19 (model-manifest.json source_ids).

Every package source is cited per record (exercises.json source_ids), never per muscle cell, and with no locator or limitation; our standard needs a source with a locator and a limitation on every mapping (10-multi-region.md section 8; 05-mappings.md line 34).
fa-45, fa-46 and fa-49 list A02 twice in source_ids (Exercise-review-ledger.md lines 890, 909, 966).
Every rep profile (rep-profiles.json) cites the same five sources S09, S10, S11, S14, S18, whether wrist, rotation, elbow, finger, thumb, hold or ballistic.

new.title: Loyola upper extremity muscle table
new.searchCheck: Not found: no result returned this PDF or its URL. Other regions' research dossiers cite LUMEN pages on mirror hosts (meddean.luc.edu dissector pages, docs/specialization-atlas/regions/upper_arm/research/dossier.json:1141-1146), not this file.
new.couldSupport: A second anatomy reference for the four forearm function claims that rest on one source (fcu.function A8, pl.function A9, ecrb.function A29, ecu.function A31; 03-anatomy-evidence.md:23), and an action reference for mappings now resting on S4, which never appeared in search (03-anatomy-evidence.md:35; 251 mappings).
new.blocker: Its text cannot be checked here; cite only after a search excerpt supports the sentence, per 03-anatomy-evidence.md section 1.

new.title: Electromyographic activity and strength during maximum isometric pronation and supination efforts in healthy adults
new.searchCheck: Citation confirmed through a later paper's reference list: Gordon KD, Pardo RD, Johnson JA, King GJ, Miller TA, J Orthop Res 2004;22(1):208-213. No abstract was returned, so neither the PubMed id, the fine-wire method nor the 'PQ active in both directions' finding was confirmed.
new.couldSupport: A new pq claim (PQ active in supination as well as pronation) and, if the abstract says so, a reviewed stabilizer mapping cat-406:forearm.pq (the package's fa-18 PQ supporting_isometric); a second EMG source beside M5 (pilot, n=4) and M6 for the shared PT/PQ (405) and supinator/biceps (406) mappings (mappings.ts:279-284). 03-anatomy-evidence.md:149 says no source separating PT and PQ was found.
new.blocker: Abstract not seen; maximal isometric efforts, not repetitions.

new.title: Characterizing forearm muscle activity in university-aged males during dynamic radial-ulnar deviation of the wrist using a wrist robot
new.searchCheck: Confirmed: Forman et al., J Biomech 2020;108:109897. Abstract: 12 males, surface EMG of eight muscles, a wrist robot applying radial or ulnar torque in 30 deg supination, neutral or 30 deg pronation; posture mainly affected the muscles acting on the hand, phase and torque direction nearly all; extensor carpi radialis the most task dependent; co-contraction ratios much higher in radial trials, suggesting FCU and ECU stabilize the wrist.
new.couldSupport: An EMG citation for the deviation mappings 407 and 408, now anatomy only (mappings.ts:228-233, 275-276); a selectivity claim on ECR task dependence; a candidate draft stabilizer role for FCU and ECU in radial deviation.
new.blocker: Robot handle task, not a dumbbell lever; surface EMG; acute; males only.

new.title: The effects of isometric hand grip force on wrist kinematics and forearm muscle activity during radial and ulnar wrist joint perturbations
new.searchCheck: Confirmed: Mannella, Forman, Mugnosso, Zenzeri, Holmes, PeerJ 2022 (PMC9138088). Abstract: 20 adults, surface EMG of eight upper-extremity muscles, robotic radial and ulnar perturbations at four grip levels; activity rose with grip force in all muscles, before and after perturbation; activity greater in ulnar than radial deviation.
new.couldSupport: A second source beside M2 for the wrist-extensor stabilizer mappings of 135, 136, 145, 299, 409 (mappings.ts:122-130, 307); the evidence the package leans on for FCR/FCU and extensor stabilizer cells in hangs, curls, rows and levers (all PACKAGE-ONLY in reconciliation.json).
new.blocker: Which eight muscles were recorded was not confirmed; perturbation with a controlled grip, not a hang, carry or curl: an analogy, so a new stabilizer mapping it supports is 'inference', not 'emg'.

new.title: Impact of Fat Grip Attachments on Muscular Strength and Neuromuscular Activation During Resistance Exercise
new.searchCheck: Confirmed: Krings et al., J Strength Cond Res 2021;35(Suppl 1). Abstract: 15 trained men; 1RM fell with the attachment on every exercise and pull-ups were fewer; forearm and shoulder EMG rose and upper-arm EMG fell in the deadlift, bent-over row and pull-up; no EMG difference in the upright row or the concentration curl.
new.couldSupport: The rationale for any thick-handle record (fa-08, fa-09, fa-21, fa-44): no blanket multiplier; and it does not support the package's fa-08 BR grade 4 (no forearm EMG change in the curl it tested).
new.blocker: No thick-handle value exists in the variant vocabulary (types.ts:278-280; variants/dimensions.ts:86-95).

new.title: Neither load nor systemic hormones determine resistance training-mediated hypertrophy or strength gains in resistance-trained young men
new.searchCheck: Confirmed: Morton et al., J Appl Physiol 2016;121(1):129-138 (PMC4967245); 49 trained men, 12 weeks, sets to volitional fatigue; relative load did not determine hypertrophy.
new.couldSupport: Rep-range copy for the stack designer's defaults (rep-profiles.json); no atlas claim or mapping.

new.title: Effects of different intensities of resistance training with equated volume load on muscle strength and hypertrophy
new.searchCheck: Bibliographic details confirmed (Lasevicius et al., Eur J Sport Sci 2018;18(6):772-780); the abstract was not returned. A blog summary (not citable) says 20/40/60/80% 1RM, leg extension and biceps curl.
new.couldSupport: Rep/load copy for the stack designer; no atlas claim or mapping.

new.title: Cross-education after high-frequency versus low-frequency volume-matched handgrip training
new.searchCheck: Title confirmed (SciSpace author listing); journal, year and PubMed id not confirmed. A related conference abstract: both frequencies gave cross-education and similar trained-limb hypertrophy.
new.couldSupport: Frequency copy for distributing hold work across days; no atlas claim or mapping.
new.blocker: Journal and PMID unconfirmed; small, four weeks.

new.title: Isometric training and long-term adaptations: Effects of muscle length, intensity, and intent: A systematic review
new.searchCheck: Confirmed: Oranchuk, Storey, Nelson, Cronin, Scand J Med Sci Sports 2019;29(4):484-503. Abstract: hypertrophy and maximal force at any intensity; long muscle lengths more hypertrophy; high-intensity (>=70%) contractions needed for tendon structure and function; few studies.
new.couldSupport: The existing rule text 'hold seconds are never converted into sets' (rules.ts:34) and hold defaults; tendon-exposure copy. No mapping.

new.title: Mechanical, Material and Morphological Adaptations of Healthy Lower Limb Tendons to Mechanical Loading: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
new.searchCheck: Confirmed: Lazarczuk et al., Sports Med 2022;52:2405-2429 (PMC9474511); objectives only, results not returned.
new.couldSupport: Tendon-exposure copy only ('loading can adapt tendons'; lower limb).

new.title: The association between combination of hand force and forearm posture and incidence of lateral epicondylitis in a working population
new.searchCheck: Title and a February 2014 prospective-study record confirmed (CDC stacks); journal (DOI points to Human Factors) and results not returned.
new.couldSupport: Tendon-exposure copy for a lateral-elbow view; never a risk number (rules.ts:41).

new.title: Quantitative Measures of Physical Risk Factors Associated with Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders of the Elbow: A Systematic Review
new.searchCheck: Confirmed: Seidel et al., IJERPH 2019;16:130 (PMC6339038); 10 studies 2007-2017, 133 risk-factor specifications, e.g. forearm supination >=45 deg with forceful lifting.
new.couldSupport: Tendon-exposure copy (why posture and force are recorded); never a threshold.
